# Research question

When do thermodynamic and interphase-model choices change predicted capture and
axial temperature, and which numerical methods resolve those changes efficiently?
The submitted revision is preserved separately. This notebook organizes retained
findings and possible next studies; no new column calculation was performed during
branch consolidation.

# Select the calculation explicitly

A study TOML file selects a formulation, thermodynamic model, film closure,
method, cases and numerical settings. Preview prints the selection without
importing the model. Execution requires `--run` and a new output directory.

```bash
python3 src/mea_absorption_column/research.py --list-options
python3 src/mea_absorption_column/research.py analyses/research_options/options.toml
```

| Formulation | Implemented selections | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Seven-state column | Henry, neutral/ionic ePC-SAFT or nine-species reactive ePC-SAFT; explicit/implicit enhancement or supplied film linearization; shooting, SciPy BVP or finite differences | Existing column balances and empirical calorics, with explicitly selected closures |
| Conserved balances supplied by a study | Trapezoidal, centered, shooting or adaptive collocation | The builder supplies compatible thermodynamics, film, balances and boundaries; a method change need not change those equations |
| Twelve-state coupled-column experiment | Preserved source and numerical evidence at `archive/coupled-solver-2026-09-08` | Not yet integrated with the shared seven-state derivative/caloric interface |

A linearized film profile is a frozen input to an outer iteration. It is not a
solved film at every new column state. Native derivatives currently cover the
explicit-enhancement seven-state path; unsupported derivative combinations fail
rather than masquerade as an exact Jacobian. Estimated parameters and preliminary
methods remain usable research topics without being labelled validated.

# Retained findings and potential promotions

| Study | Retained finding | Next discriminating work |
|---|---|---|
| Submitted nine-species column | Seven-case evaluation, Case 3C refinement and sensitivity studies are retained on `codex/fallback-manuscript` | Use as a stated reference when relevant; it does not define every research case |
| Equilibrium-manifold film campaign | Film capture MAE 6.700 percentage points versus 4.038 for its enhancement comparator; estimated mobility and mixed bulk/film changes limit interpretation | Separate bulk-thermodynamic changes from film changes on common inputs before attributing improvement |
| Film numerical reachability | One provisional state completed after 592.179 s, six iterations and 355 points; kinetics/diffusivities were unresolved | Resolve physical inputs before interpreting the computed flux as an experimental prediction |
| CasADi RHS comparison | A value-only callback did not supply the required total derivative; disposable finite-difference trials did not establish the target speedup | Use an explicitly differentiable formulation; compare cost at matched numerical accuracy |
| Conservative-method development | Analytic checks and consistent single-node recovery are retained; a full-column method ranking is absent | Establish a coherent coupled builder and converged trajectory before a physical timing/refinement comparison |
| MDEA and eNRTL | MDEA interface groundwork is retained, but neither is an integrated selectable column model here | Supply equations, parameter/reaction bases and mapped observations before claiming a comparable model |

# Comparison design

Change one specified closure at a time when interpreting its effect. Compare
common feed bases, geometry, transport assumptions and reaction definitions;
then investigate their interactions explicitly. Keep numerical residuals,
conservation, profile refinement, observed agreement and runtime scope separate.
A model may converge and still disagree with observations. A timeout is a measured
budget outcome, not evidence that the physical equations have no solution.

# Working practice

Create a study configuration, run it separately into a new directory, inspect its
results and failures, then update an analysis notebook. Render with execution
disabled. Candidate promotions should state the scientific question, exact inputs,
method, checks, uncertainty and what remains unexplained. Manuscript editing is
outside this research phase.

# Seven-state Engine calculation: numerical verification

Case 3C with ionic ePC-SAFT fugacity returns **92.08186315973761% CO2
capture**, using the pinned Engine 1.0.0 wheel from commit
`f4566b3d0c64d05822b41fe363de47ab5cfa6a0e`, SHA-256
`57bdf6c4277722fdf378107fa940fd321a4e9caeed8875165a27c318239dbd4a`.
This is numerical verification of the existing seven-state equations, not
physical validation or an isolated thermodynamic-model comparison.

The input is `C_cases_data/3C`, molar conversion, `legacy_ratio` vapor
composition and `reported_total_wet` gas flow: liquid CO2/MEA/water feeds
2.5639189042486694/10.255675616994678/81.1120360118802 mol/s; vapor
CO2/water/N2/O2 feeds 1.53499705118/1.47758972194387/15.133559109341697/
1.2841965375344333 mol/s. Liquid and vapor enter at 318.15 and 316.75 K;
packed height is 6 m, area 0.3216990877275948 m², and constant pressure
109500 Pa. The equations use legacy chemical equilibrium, empirical enthalpy
states, explicit enhancement, raw states and numerical derivatives. No
thermodynamic parameters or transport equations changed.

SciPy boundary-value collocation used 21 starting nodes, tolerance 0.5,
boundary tolerance 0.001 and at most 1000 nodes. It returned 22 nodes after
two iterations in 4.178 s within `execution.wall_limit_s = 600`.
Maximum collocation RMS residual is 0.22481082656001908; maximum scaled
boundary residual is 1.6940658945086007e-21. The separate boundary residual
percent norm is 6.915441663935132e-14. The loose collocation tolerance does
not establish profile refinement or capture accuracy.

With both stream flows represented as positive magnitudes and liquid flowing
toward decreasing height, the conserved differences are liquid minus vapor.
Maximum drift from the bottom native node is:

| Quantity | Absolute drift | Relative drift and normalization |
|---|---:|---:|
| CO2 flow difference | 4.440892098500626e-16 mol/s | 2.893094872779576e-16 / inlet vapor CO2 |
| Water flow difference | 9.242739906767383e-11 mol/s | 6.255281672241147e-11 / inlet vapor water |
| Enthalpy-flow difference | 2.905726432800293e-7 W | 6.171416760085979e-14 / maximum inlet enthalpy-flow magnitude |
| Pressure | 0 Pa | 0 / specified pressure |

The retained seven-state ionic row for 3C in
`analyses/nccc_validation/results/final/tables/raw_c_case_thermo_benchmark.csv`
reports 88.74708790292281% capture: the new result is higher by
3.334775256814794 percentage points. That row points to
`c_case_campaign_temperature_overlay_metrics.csv`; its complete numerical
settings and wheel identity are absent from the table. This comparison does
not isolate an Engine effect or establish numerical preservation. Capture
and conservation here are a few scalar quantities, so a table states the
comparison without implying a resolved trend.

Reproduce with `uv run --frozen python src/mea_absorption_column/research.py
analyses/research_options/inputs/engine_ionic_3c.toml --run`, choosing a new
output directory. The retained result is
[attempt.json](results/runs/engine_ionic_3c_verified_20261029/attempt.json), with
[conservation and comparison values](results/runs/engine_ionic_3c_verified_20261029/conservation_comparison.json)
and [run log](results/runs/engine_ionic_3c_verified_20261029/run.log).
The balance-report command in `scripts/check_seven_state_balances.py` reads
this retained native profile without running the model. A preceding repeat
in `results/runs/engine_ionic_3c_20261029/attempt.json` returned the identical
capture and residuals in 5.372 s.

The three distinct persistent checks use both ionic and nine-species reactive
Engine fugacity: extensive-enthalpy directional differences test temperature
inversion and chain factors; prescribed fluxes test the smooth-cap derivative
across absorption and desorption; and nonzero area factors, including both
clipped limits, test material and energy scaling and conservation. These
checks establish neither native derivatives for those optional closures nor
physical accuracy. The calculation and notebook have not been independently
reviewed or promoted for manuscript use.

All 18 new checks pass. Disposable mutations (a 1 K liquid-temperature
inversion error, replacing the smooth cap by a hard cap, and ignoring the
area factor) fail the corresponding checks; the retained source was not
modified for those probes. These checks expose distinct numerical errors
rather than merely exercising the selected functions.
